title: Mictlāntēcutli: what the underworld keeps spelled right

# Mictlāntēcutli: what the underworld keeps spelled right
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Mictlāntēcutli** stay *mictlantecutli*.

Mictlāntēcutli's myths are few but pivotal. He guards the bones of the previous creation, and the future of humankind depends on outwitting him. After the Fourth Sun perished, Quetzalcōātl descended into Mictlān to retrieve the bones of earlier humans so that the gods could fashion a new race.  Mictlāntēcutli agreed, on condition that Quetzalcōātl walk four times around his realm blowing a conch shell that had no holes.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Mictlāntēcutli
- **ASCII form:** mictlantecutli
- **Meaning:** "Lord of the Land of the Dead"
- **Domain of influence:** Lord of Mictlān, Death, Underworld
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 151 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Mictlāntēcutli** to *mictlantecutli* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.
- **e → ē** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Mictlāntēcutli** lives at [/sites/mictlantecutli/](/sites/mictlantecutli/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/mictlantecutli/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/mictlantecutli/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/mictlantecutli/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Mictlāntēcutli** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — Lord of the land of the dead; the Mexica afterlife’s keeper.
- **Music, Arts & Performance** — Metal bands, muralists, and cartoonists return to him as the dignified keeper of mortality; the skull aesthetic of whole genres descends from his death cult.
- **Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services** — The keeper of the dead whom Quetzalcōātl had to outwit; necromancy, the esoteric economy's oldest practice, is the art of treating with him.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
